pages.title: The Burn Line
pages.scene: Burnt strip, Ashen Leaf border road
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: Twenty paces of forest gone to black stubble, ruled off neat between two boundary stones. Fires don't usually mind property lines.
A courier sits on the eastern stone, one sleeve burned to the elbow, sorting scorched letters by weight.
She has been waving travelers through all morning. You, she stands up for.

pages.title: Undeliverable
pages.speaker: Pell Marrow
dialogue: Pell Marrow, courier. I need somebody outside both patrol units to carry what I saw past the rope.
This dispatch says Frostfang burned the strip. I was standing in it when it caught. I don't deliver things I watched be wrong.
Two patrols came to the light. Both in correct marks. Frostfang wool, Ashen Leaf gray. Patrols don't share a fire.
There's a witness. Charcoal-burner up the ridge, Umi. Get to her before the captains do.
Ask her about the second patrol twice. Not once. Twice. You'll see.

pages.title: Ask Her Twice
pages.speaker: Umi
dialogue: I don't sleep when the kilns are banked. Saw the whole thing. Two patrols, plain as washing on a line.
First lot wore Frostfang wool, seal-marks at the wrist. Second lot was Ashen Leaf gray, register braids. Stood right where you're standing.
The second lot? Frostfang, I said. Blue wool, wrist-marks. Why do you keep... I said that. Didn't I say that.
There was a comfort-man through here after the fire. Took the worst of that night off me for two coins. Cheap, I thought.
Odd, though. I can tell you every button on the first patrol. The second lot's faces come up smooth. Like river stones.
Kiln three wants feeding. Mind the sparks going down.

pages.title: Lead in the Ash
pages.speaker: Pell Marrow
dialogue: Found this raking the ash while you were up the ridge. Lead tally-token. The Red Tally chit their bridge crews with these.
They hold the toll bridge at Corrom. Burn a strip here, both villages posture, and every caravan reroutes over their planks. Paying.
Both patrol captains reach the stones at dusk. Frostfang's side is already drafting a protest with blood in the margins.
Whatever you do with this token, do it knowing they'll both watch how it's done. Border people keep long books.
Your call. I just carry things.

choices.text: Show both captains the token, then hunt the Tally burners
choices.conclusion: The captains countersign a joint report before the protest is finished being angry; Frostfang's patrol stands down at the stones. Pell points you up the Corrom bridge road, where the Red Tally are still counting reroute tolls.

choices.text: Seal the token and carry it to Elder Mori unannounced
choices.conclusion: Mori reads it twice, files it under something unrelated, and thanks you for the weather report. By morning both patrols are recalled without a reason given, and no protest is ever posted.

choices.text: Press the token into a Saltbrand freight crate at the crossing
choices.conclusion: Within the week both villages are paying for armed escorts against Saltbrand wagons, and an unsigned retainer finds your camp. Umi tells the story with Saltbrand in it now, and believes every word.

pages.title: The Watcher at the Rail
pages.scene: A waystation yard off the north road
pages.speaker: Instructor Havek
dialogue: You. Take the practice rail once. I want to see what your guard does when the strike comes from the left.
There. Fourth exchange. Nobody covered it because nobody was paired with you.
Frostfang drills for exactly that. Pairs. I have six students, this yard, and one hour before the road takes me north.
First lesson is paid: one hour holding pads for my six students. What you learn while doing it is yours.

pages.title: Drill Twelve
pages.speaker: Petra
dialogue: Hold out your wrist. Habit, sorry. We check marks at home. Whatever yours says, Havek says the yard rule is the same for everyone.
Stand closer. If I can't touch your shoulder, I can't cover you. That's drill one.
The scroll's older than Havek. Except drill twelve. The ink runs darker there.
He swears his instructor taught him twelve. His instructor swears she never did.
Anyway. Elbows in.

pages.title: The Mask in the Yard
pages.scene: Dust, scattered pads, one figure running
pages.speaker: Instructor Havek
dialogue: Down! Mask in the yard. He sat through the whole drill. Count off!
Petra, second pair, behind the well. That is not a request, it's drill four.
He has the scroll.
Twenty years of drills in one hand and my students in the open. Choose fast, stranger. I already know my answer.

pages.title: The Open Gate
pages.scene: The yard gate, the thief clearing it
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: The mask clears the fence, scroll under one arm. The students are strung out across the yard, unpaired.
Havek is already moving, toward the youngest of them, not the thief.
The gate stands open. The road north is dry and fast.

choices.text: Pull the scattered students behind you and hold the yard.
choices.conclusion: The mask is gone north before the dust settles. Havek counts his students twice, writes your name at the bottom of his roster, and mentions he works this road every month.

choices.text: Split the pairs: half guard the yard, half cut the road.
choices.conclusion: The pairs peel off clean, like they had drilled it. You take the road side alone, and at the treeline the mask stops running and turns, scroll strapped tight.

choices.text: Rip the scroll from the thief's grip and keep it.
choices.conclusion: The mask gives the scroll up strangely easily and is over the fence without looking back. Havek rolls his sleeve past the oath-mark and steps between you and the gate. 'Village property. Drill nineteen covers retrieval.'

pages.title: The Rubbings
pages.speaker: Oren Slate
dialogue: Three sectors. Same boot, same stride, same hour. I took rubbings. Look.
Frostfang winter tread, size nine, heavy on the left heel. In Reedmarsh he's running east.
In Coldbrook, same hour, running west. Downhill both times. Don't start about hills. I checked the hills.
I've tracked liars, corpses, a bear that swam a river to spite me. Never a man who's three men at once.
You walk roads that don't behave. That's why I waved you over. Well. Most of why.

pages.title: The Print That Starts Nowhere
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: The trail begins in the middle of the field. No approach. No landing. Eleven strides, then nothing.
The toe digs deep, like a sprint. The spacing says a walk. Both can't be true. Both are.
Inside each print the mud has frozen. It is the sixth week of summer.
A crow works the far hedge, uninterested.

pages.title: Everywhere He Isn't
pages.speaker: Oren Slate
dialogue: A fresh print appeared while I ate lunch. There was no one there. I only saw the mud sink.
I don't think these prints show where he is. They show all the places he's afraid we'll search.
Boot roll came back from a Frostfang quartermaster. Drawn by one Dess Havel. Marked absent at roll call, twice.
His fear is leaving tracks even when his body isn't there.
I've never seen anything like it.

pages.title: Your Road
pages.speaker: Oren Slate
dialogue: Frostfang hunters cross the border tomorrow. They'll follow prints. The prints go everywhere he isn't.
Lucky for Havel. It won't stay lucky. Terror this loud draws worse than hunters.
I read ground. I can't read a frightened man's spillage. You maybe can.
And if you can't, I'd put my fee on %pet. I've watched the two of you walk all day. Not one wrong step between you.
So. Your road. What do we do with it?

choices.text: Track the fear backward to the man himself
choices.conclusion: You find Havel folded into a culvert two sectors from any print and sit with him until his breathing slows; across three sectors, frozen mud goes soft. Oren burns his rubbings without being asked.

choices.text: Seal the freshest print into a warding charm
choices.conclusion: Oren holds the wax while you press the print in; the charm twitches now whenever someone nearby is running scared. He asks, carefully, what you'd charge for a second one.

choices.text: Study how the terror lands, and practice aiming it
choices.conclusion: You learn the throw: fear lands where the runner's head goes, and a head can be steered. By dark, size-nine prints walk straight through the hunters' camp, and Oren leaves without collecting his fee.

pages.title: The Wall Side
pages.scene: Switchback trail above the salt flats
pages.speaker: Serel
dialogue: You passed me twice on the switchbacks. Both times you took the drop side and left me the wall.
Most walkers take the wall. It's shade. It's the whole reason to start that hour early.
There's a stone half a day north that opens for maybe one walker in a hundred. I've started guessing which ones. I'm usually wrong.
Come north. Prove me wrong again or don't.
Mind the shale on the third bend.

pages.title: The Stone
pages.scene: A lidded stone in dry scrub
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: The lid carries no tool marks. Its seam is finer than a hair and holds no dust.
Moss circles it at arm's length, a ring in no pattern anyone planted.
The sun side of the stone is cold. The shaded side is warm.
%pet stops at the moss line unasked and stays there, watching the seam.
Serel sets her pack down outside the ring and stays standing.

pages.title: Three Dry Days
pages.speaker: Serel
dialogue: Three days I've walked dry. On purpose. Watch the seam, not me.
There's water at my lip right now. I want it more than most things I can name.
The stone can tell the difference between having nothing and refusing something you could take. Anholt made me learn that while I was thirsty, so I'm showing you the same way.
Watch the dust along the seam. It moves when someone makes that choice.
Anholt called the makers Ancients, people from the Sunken Court's age. The ones who refused cession, he called the Withheld.
Now I drink.

pages.title: Your Own No
pages.speaker: Serel
dialogue: It opened for me once, a long walk ago. I read what's in there and put it back.
It shut when I picked up my pack. No offense taken either way. That's the manner of it.
It will want a no of your own. Mine's spent.
Whatever you do, do it where I can see. Somebody should be able to say what happened here.
I'll be in the shade, eating. Don't read anything into that.

choices.text: Refuse tonight's meal and wait at the seam
choices.conclusion: At dusk the seam parts on a slate of names, each beside the one thing its owner refused to cede. You read until the light goes and set it back. As the seam closes, a glyph surfaces beside your hand: the same cut that marks older acts of refusal, not a name or a Bloodline sign. Serel checks it against her staff. 'Same cut. Somebody saw you say no.'

choices.text: Measure the stone, copy its rule, touch nothing
choices.conclusion: You sketch the ring, the seam, the cold sun side, and write the rule beneath: opens for a refusal, witnessed. Serel corrects your moss line by a handspan and walks you back to the road.

choices.text: Drive a chisel into the seam and pry
choices.conclusion: By the third strike the seam is gone and the stone is one smooth piece. You cairn the spot for a return with better tools, and Serel shoulders her pack without a word.

events.title: The Shrine That Both Sides Own

pages.title: The Count at the Door
pages.scene: Mud road below the shrine pass
pages.speaker: Sefa
dialogue: Sefa, shrine road. Whatever flag you carry, keep it covered while I talk; both lines are watching for an excuse.
Storm banners on the west steps of the shrine. Ash banners east. Horns twice since dawn.
Nine villagers are still inside. I count sandals at the door. Eleven went up; nine pairs are still sitting there.
Old Maru's knees quit on the climb. He is not coming down without help, and I am done being polite about it.

pages.title: The Shrine Between Banners
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: The shrine controls the narrowest point of the pass. Every patrol, courier, and traveler moves beneath its steps.
At dusk, shrine keepers and passing shinobi leave rice wine in the offering bowl. By dawn it is gone, and neither village admits whose watch drank first.
Both founders' names are carved on the inner wall. Stormveil reads its own, Ashen Leaf reads its own. One wall. One hand cut both names before either village drew this border.
Sefa's people sweep the steps every morning. Before sunrise, someone cleared away blood and bootprints.

pages.title: The West Line
pages.speaker: Captain Hela Dray
dialogue: You. State your business, pick a step, or clear the pass.
That hill takes toll off Stormveil roads. Ash walls it up, we take it back. Simple as weather.
The civilians climbed on their own. Doors open when the fighting stops. Tell them to quit ringing that bell.
Cross my line, that's a challenge. I honor challenges. Ask whoever's still standing.

pages.title: The East Line
pages.scene: East steps, behind the ash banners
pages.speaker: Warden Suvi Rell
dialogue: My mother's name is on that wall. She holds this pass. I only carry the permit.
Dray calls it a toll hill. The register calls it our first page. Neither founder carved that wall, which nobody says on the steps.
If she puts fire to those names, they go where... no. State your business or stand clear.
Mind the third step. It ices, even in summer.

pages.title: Nine Pairs of Sandals
pages.speaker: Sefa
dialogue: West side is dipping arrows in pitch. I watched the girl with the pot do it twice.
Nine pairs of sandals. Old Maru cannot run. Little Essa will not leave him.
Dray wants the hill, Rell wants the wall, and the bowl just wants filling. Same as every dusk.
Horns again. So. Are you here for the nine people, or for one of the banners?

choices.text: Lead the civilians out and call both commanders down
choices.conclusion: You come down with Old Maru on your back and eight behind you, and the arrows hold, because loosing one now means shooting you. Rell grounds her banners; Dray steps into the pass and rolls her shoulders.

choices.text: Broker terms: split hours, banners down, bowl sealed
choices.conclusion: Rell copies the terms into her register before Dray finishes carving her mark into the step: dawn hours west, dusk hours east, the bowl sealed in its niche behind both villages' wax. Sefa relights the lamps that night.

choices.text: Slip inside and pocket the bowl while they argue
choices.conclusion: By nightfall each village swears the other lifted it, and the pass grows two new checkpoints. Sefa counts what leaves shrines the way she counts sandals, and she watched your hands.

pages.title: The Stone at the Fork
pages.scene: A marker stone where three roads meet
pages.speaker: Emissary Corvane
dialogue: You stopped to read the stone. Good.
West of here there was a ford, a war, and one act in the middle of both.
Three people watched. Three accounts survive. They cannot all be the same act.
A Legacy is not an ancestor coming back, and it is not something sleeping in a Bloodline. In the Sunken Court's age, people later called the Withheld refused to cede one defining choice.

What survived was the shape of the choice. Across old accounts, witnesses kept recognizing the same hundred patterns: mercy, calculation, ambition, endurance. A Legacy returns when someone freely repeats one under witness.
Isa's descendants do not own one. But this family has repeated her disputed act for generations. Which pattern they teach depends on which account is true, and her name is missing from all three.
Start with the miller at the west ford. He keeps a tin he thinks is the point.

pages.title: What the Miller Keeps
pages.scene: A millhouse loft above the west ford
pages.speaker: Bracken
dialogue: We were what was left of the Redwillow column. Forty walking wounded on the wrong side of the water.
She came out of the trees alone, and I thought, that's the end of us. Then she knelt and tested the ice.
Every step, her own weight first. Walked forty enemies across like a shepherd who hated counting.
At the far bank she gave my brother her rations. Then she crossed back and stood guard, so her own side would see her do it.
Mercy. Whatever the sergeant tells you, write mercy.
Tin's on that shelf. My brother kept it. Thirty winters and it never once rusted.

pages.title: The Sergeant's Arithmetic
pages.scene: A porch in a border hamlet
pages.speaker: Sergeant Venn
dialogue: Mercy? Bracken said mercy. Of course he did. He was fed.
Their side held eleven of ours in the Redwillow stockade. Forty of theirs stood on our ice. Do the sum yourself.
By thaw, our eleven walked home. Nobody signed anything. That is what the good trades look like.
I told the inquiry I'd have made the same call. The inquiry wasn't about the call.
They offered her a captaincy for holding the ford. Holding it. She stood up in front of everyone and corrected the record.
Her name was Isa Renn. There. Now somebody besides me can say it.

pages.title: The Ninth of Thaw
pages.speaker: Emissary Corvane
dialogue: The third witness died a captain. Her deposition outlived her. Quartermaster Sesh, supply clerk at Redwillow.
'She let them cross so their commander would owe her. She wanted rank. Ambition, plain as ink.' That is the whole of it.
It is dated the ninth of Thaw. That Thaw ran eight days. No one at any register can tell me where the ninth went.
And the page where Isa Renn sat is smooth. A burned name scars the paper. Hers left nothing to scar.
Sesh took the captaincy she turned down. Held it eleven years. Died respected.
Three versions are out walking, wearing one woman. Come to Ashen Leaf and decide which one keeps walking.

pages.title: The Open Register
pages.scene: The register hall in Ashen Leaf, after hours
pages.speaker: Emissary Corvane
dialogue: The registrar let me open the book after hours. The pen is yours.
Think before you write. Mercy done for a reward is different from mercy done because someone needed help.
Tomorrow the registrar copies your entry onto the road notice. Isa's family will read it before noon.
Whatever you enter here will become the version people repeat.
Write.

choices.text: Write the ford back into the register under Isa Renn's name.
choices.conclusion: The registrar copies the entry twice, then sends for ash to set the name in new mortar. Corvane bows to the page, not to you.

choices.text: Copy all three accounts into the book, side by side, unsigned.
choices.conclusion: The registrar files the versions facing one another. Corvane reads the first, then the second, then the third. He leaves the book open and asks for another lamp.

choices.text: Claim Sesh's version. Let the road believe the ford was yours.
choices.conclusion: By the next waystation a carter is already telling it with your description in it. Corvane closes the book unsigned and says borrowed patterns run small at the shoulders.

pages.title: The Convoy
pages.scene: Cart track above a drowned tollhouse
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: Two wagons, five guards, and one crate lashed down with more rope than a crate needs.
The mules will pull behind it but not ahead of it. The drivers have stopped arguing with them.
Kite Harrow sits on the tailboard, boots crossed, reading a contract she has already read.
She waves you over like the two of you planned this.

pages.title: Hazard Rate
pages.speaker: Kite Harrow
dialogue: Kite Harrow. If we have met, I charged you. If we have not, take this as the free introduction.
I'm escorting sealed cargo for six days. Your village is listed as a hostile party, so technically you're the hazard I'm being paid for.
I haven't opened the crate. My contract charges extra for inspection, and nobody approved the fee.
But I weigh it every morning. It's getting heavier.
Grain can settle and stone doesn't change. This cargo is doing something else.

pages.title: The Tallyman
pages.scene: Head of the convoy, ledger open
pages.speaker: Bellis Crane
dialogue: Is there a problem? The cargo is grain futures and quarry samples for the northern account.
The cargo is grain futures and quarry samples for the northern account.
...You asked twice. People keep asking me twice lately. I don't see why.
If the contractor concerns you, the company pays an informant fee. Two hundred, standing. It's posted at every waystation.
We move at the half bell. Mind the mules.

pages.title: The Menu
pages.speaker: Kite Harrow
dialogue: You heard it too. He repeats that sentence with the same words and the same breath every time.
I only have the contract, and something is wrong with it.
If I break the seal, I pay the penalty. We can split it, or I can owe you a favor for staying quiet.
You could also report me to Bellis and take the two hundred.
Whatever is in the crate, I think the real cost was taken from someone who doesn't know about it.

choices.text: Break the seal with her; split the penalty
choices.conclusion: Inside are clay tallies stamped with living names and RECEIVED IN FULL. Beneath them lies an older slab. Each family line appears twice: first as COMPLIANT, UNSTABLE, or LINEAGE UNCONFIRMED, then beside a single trait the Court meant to extract. Strongest. Cruelest. Most loyal. Harrow reads the list twice. 'This isn't a Legacy registry. It's an intake list. Somebody was pricing what could be taken from a person.' She copies the names, then nails the manifest to the waystation board.

choices.text: Trade your silence for a favor in her ledger
choices.conclusion: She writes one line: favor owed, no expiry, your name spelled right, and shows you before closing the book. The crate rolls on, and the mules still won't walk ahead of it.

choices.text: Report her to Bellis; collect the two hundred
choices.conclusion: Bellis counts out two hundred and voids her contract on the spot, penalty and all. Harrow watches you pocket it, then opens her ledger and writes something short.

pages.title: A Name Both Sides Gave
pages.scene: Toll road above the Grey Fork
pages.speaker: Registrar Corin Vell
dialogue: Both delegations gave your name as a witness outside their exchange units. Independently, which never happens. I checked twice.
Prisoner exchange at Black Bridge, noon. Six of Frostfang's for one of Moonshadow's. On paper, anyway.
I record it. I don't guarantee it. There's a difference, and it's usually about a hundred paces wide.
They wanted a witness neither side commands for this exchange. That is all I am vouching for.
Bring nothing that gleams. The bridge has rooflines on both banks.

pages.title: The Count
pages.speaker: Sergeant Aldis Rime
dialogue: Six names. Berrit, Ost, Kanna Fole, the twins, Hedge. I call, they answer, they cross.
Moonshadow brought a covered cart for one man. One. That's either respect or a coffin.
Berrit's wrist mark reads wrong. He keeps saying he walked here. He didn't. We logged his capture. I have the log.
Protocol says I don't watch their rooftops. So you watch them.
Wind's from the east. Noted.

pages.title: The Chalk Lines
pages.speaker: Veil Adaza
dialogue: The sergeant counts them like coins. Do you suppose they count back?
Our man crosses last. You want to know why. Do you want to owe me for the answer?
The registrar vouched for you. What did that cost him, I wonder.
Something's wrong with the light on the mill roof. Or nothing is. Notice how those feel the same?
Four names called. Two to go.

pages.title: First Bolt
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: A crossbow bolt comes off the mill roof and drops Rime's second mid-count. Kanna Fole never gets to answer her name.
Both escorts draw. The prisoners stand chained in the open between the chalk lines, belonging to nobody.
On the roofline, one figure, already reloading. Along both banks, low shapes moving toward the bridge mouth.
Vell is still writing. His hand hasn't stopped once.

choices.text: Put yourself between the bolts and the chained.
choices.conclusion: The shooter slides off the far roofline and is gone; six prisoners and one ledger-keeper crouch behind you, breathing. Vell writes your name on the exchange record's first line, above both villages.

choices.text: Hold both lines to the count; track the shooter after.
choices.conclusion: The exchange finishes ugly but whole, and by evening you've found the perch: flattened moss, a tea flask stamped with a mill mark. Vell files the exchange as clean and your finding in the margin, initialed.

choices.text: Run the shooter down and price what they know.
choices.conclusion: The shooter gives up the hirer's name inside an hour, and by dusk you've sold it to the delegation that paid better. Adaza opens a ledger line under your name, and that is not a courtesy.

pages.title: The Paid Lesson
pages.scene: Waystation yard, frost on the rails
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: A Frostfang challenger waits at the waystation with chalk and a fee paid up front, both halves, winner's and loser's.
She asked the keeper for the strongest hand on the road. He named you before she finished asking.
She chalks the ring two shoulders wide: the width of a cellar corridor.
Nobody at the station understands why she paid to learn in a space that small. She came anyway.

pages.title: Show Me Slower
pages.speaker: Anji Vesk
dialogue: Before we start. Show me a wrist break that works against somebody who knows you will try it. Slower first.
No, don't score it. I don't care where the point went. Where was your thumb?
If the ceiling is low. A cellar, say. Does the throw still clear?
Last one. How do you put a man down so he wakes up fine? He has to stand a roll call after.

pages.title: The Letters Lean Wrong
pages.scene: Fence rail, sharing a water skin
pages.speaker: Anji Vesk
dialogue: My brother packed a bag last winter. Corin. They found it at the gate before he could use it.
No trial. They walked him down to the vault and re-swore him. Standard procedure, they said. Kind, even.
He came back polite. I checked the new oath against his old one. Same hand. The letters lean the wrong way.
Mother swears he never packed a bag. She helped him fold the shirts. She swears it anyway.
Water's yours. The wrist break once at speed, then I stop buying your morning without telling you why.

pages.title: Both Halves, Up Front
pages.scene: The yard, chalk dust, new ring
pages.speaker: Anji Vesk
dialogue: He will fight me when I come for him. The mark will make him. So I will lose as many lessons as it takes to learn something useful.
Roll call is dawn and dusk. Between them, one window. I have measured everything except whether I am good enough.
First lesson. Both halves of the fee, up front.
Well.

choices.text: Take the chalk. Train her like you mean it.
choices.conclusion: She stops asking about points and asks about Corin instead. Reach, weight, which shoulder he favors. Then she chalks a fresh ring: the lesson starts now, full speed.

choices.text: Set a price: watch rotations for every lesson.
choices.conclusion: She pays without haggling: rotations, the relief pattern, which gate man drinks on duty. She logs each lesson against each fact in a two-column tablet, balanced, nothing owed.

choices.text: Break her, and make Corin your leverage.
choices.conclusion: You say Corin's name and let it sit. The keeper pulls his shutters closed; she picks up the chalk anyway.

pages.title: The Neutral Nobody Meant
pages.scene: Switchback road above the drill flats
pages.speaker: Proctor Hasse
dialogue: Both commands asked for an outside witness, then sent me private definitions of outside. I ignored both.
The Alliance Drill. Stormveil blades, Frostfang lines, forty trainees, chalk seals on every edge. One morning a year of pretending the border is a suggestion.
I proctor. I record. This year the record already has a problem in it.
The third seal crate weighed heavy against the manifest. I weighed it twice. The manifest didn't change. My memory of the first weighing did.
Come stand where I can watch what you actually do.

pages.title: Forty-One
pages.speaker: Sergeant Brekka
dialogue: Two trainees cut to the bone on scored passes. Chalk seals sting. These paid out in edge.
The flash was cold. Chalk flashes hot. I have armed nine hundred of these.
Smoke ran downhill. The wind was running up.
Roll call at dawn: forty. On the flats I count forty-one. I have counted three times.
Nobody transferred in. There would be a form.

pages.title: Stormveil Arithmetic
pages.speaker: Captain Joss Arne
dialogue: Her arithmetic's tidy. Out there my kids bleed and hers mostly don't. Run that sum.
Stormveil doesn't halt a fight for getting honest.
But somebody carved those seals wanting me to read Frostfang on them. I don't like being handed my own grudge.
So call it, witness. And call it fast. My people don't stand still well.

pages.title: A Third Hand
pages.scene: Proctor's table, the cut seal laid open
pages.speaker: Proctor Hasse
dialogue: Here is the recarved seal. The scoring hand knew both villages' work and used neither.
I pulled the border smoke file on a hunch. The cold-burn line was struck from my copy. Not redacted. Struck. Somebody tidy got there before me.
Forty-one on the flats. Two commands loading blame. One of me, and the record only counts what I survive to file.
So. What are you out here?

choices.text: Pull the trainees off the flats; show both commands the seal.
choices.conclusion: Both marshals go quiet over one recarved seal, and the forty-first bolts for the tree line. Hasse notes the time; the cell turns to meet you.

choices.text: Finish the drill clean; brief the marshals alone after.
choices.conclusion: The drill ends on the scoreboard and the alliance holds in public. By lamplight both marshals read the seal and ask, separately, whether you have ever held a sector command.

choices.text: Let the blame land on Frostfang; collect the drill honors.
choices.conclusion: Stormveil carries you off the flats while Brekka's stripes come off by nightfall. Hasse records the result exactly as witnessed, and underlines your name once.

pages.title: A Buyer, for Once
pages.scene: Toll road east of Central, dusk
pages.speaker: Corvo Latch
dialogue: Put your purse away. Today I'm the one buying.
This spring I sold a rumor. A fifth anchor under Central, older than the four. Forty buyers, clean margin.
Twenty of them pooled up and dug. Three weeks back they stopped buying rope. Then lamp oil. Then bread.
A crew that stops buying bread is dead or rich. I'd pay to know which before the villages do.
And you. People who never buy anything have started buying news of you. That made the detour cheap.

pages.title: What the Rumor Bought
pages.speaker: Foreman Dray
dialogue: Latch sent you? Then you already know what he sold us.
There's no anchor down there. There's a street. Curbstones. Door lintels. A stair cut for eight men abreast.
Three farms mortgaged for this hole, and my cousin signed over his boat. So the winch keeps turning.
One of my diggers, Kettle, has run the Hollow Gate itself twice. He came up from our gallery refusing supper, saying the air below felt the same.
Drop a stone down the far stair and the echo comes back early. Before the stone's left your hand, some nights.
Mind the third rung going down. New wood. It flexes.

pages.title: The Court Below
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: The lamp bends its light left at the lintel, as if the doorway had negotiated something with it.
Above the arch, in a script that half-survives in ledger-hand: the court below keeps its own accounts.

Under the words, columns of tallies. Each column is headed by a small carved face, and every face is asleep. Down one wall, names end. Beside scattered names, the same small marks recur centuries apart and across unrelated families: a shield, an open hand, a severed chain. Not inheritance. Repetition. The marks continue out past the lamplight.
Down the wide stair, past the lamplight, something keeps a slow rhythm. It could be water. Water doesn't count.
The third rung flexes on the way back up.

pages.title: Sold as Seen
pages.speaker: Corvo Latch
dialogue: No anchor. No refunds either. A rumor's a sold-as-seen trade, and mine was honestly false.
A verified route outsells a rumor the way a deed outsells a promise. Down there is the find of my working life.
Dray's crew won't climb out. Nobody leaves a hole with money at the bottom of it.
So. Name your position, and I'll draft the paper it needs.

choices.text: Clear the crews out and drop the shaft
choices.conclusion: You give the crew until the lamps burn down, then set charges at the winch and the gallery mouth. Dray sends his people up the ladder and stays at the bottom, mattock in hand.

choices.text: Walk the galleries, chart them, take the map to the Sage
choices.conclusion: Three days of pacing and counting turns by lamplight. Wandering Sage unrolls the map without surprise, rests a finger on the sleeping faces, and asks who else has copies.

choices.text: Verify the routes yourself and sell them at your price
choices.conclusion: Corvo has the paper drafted before you finish naming terms. By month's end two crews pay toll to walk streets nobody built for them, and your seal sits on every copy.

pages.title: Chalk Marks
pages.scene: A crossroads shrine north of Central
pages.speaker: Wandering Sage
dialogue: Good, you found me. I have four places I need you to check.
Go to the founding stones in Stormveil, Ashen Leaf, Frostfang, and Moonshadow. Look underneath each village symbol.
Take paper and a knife. If you find anything in the sockets, bring it back.
Ask your questions after you've seen all four.
There's food in the pack. The Frostfang road takes longer than the map says.

pages.title: Four Stones, One Hand
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: Stormveil's sign is a fist over a broken chain. Beneath it, cut small and deep, a hooked cross with a bar through it.
Ashen Leaf's flame. Frostfang's linked rings. Moonshadow's closed eye. Under all three, the same hooked cross. Same hand. Same depth.
Under each mark sits a socket, and in each socket a gray key that weighs more in your pack than it did in your hand.
At the fourth stone, the moss has already been scraped away.

pages.title: Someone Else's Client
pages.speaker: Kite Harrow
dialogue: Easy. I only took a rubbing. I left the key where it was.
A client paid me to prove this mark matches the one under Stormveil's stone. Paying in advance means they already knew the answer.
I can't tell you who hired me. Even I don't charge enough to take that risk.
The same person marked all four villages. Apparently nobody thought that was worth teaching us.
The Sage is waiting at the crossroads.

pages.title: One Lattice
pages.speaker: Wandering Sage
dialogue: Set all four keys down and line up the marks.
Same cut, same sockets. Whoever built these sites meant all four to meet in one older Court network. The stones cannot tell us when each village joined it.
Your villages teach freedom, memory, loyalty, and secrecy as separate virtues. To the builders, they were four doors into the same place.
The Withheld were people of that age who refused cession, not gods. Before they left, they recorded these four locks.
Witnesses use Legacy for a pattern someone chooses to repeat. It is not a Bloodline or an ancestor, and you may refuse the name.
A Kage can command the local door. These keys reach the passage beneath all four.

pages.title: What Keys Are For
pages.speaker: Wandering Sage
dialogue: Every keeper before me buried the keys again. That only worked until someone started looking for them.
If we break them, nobody can use this shortcut again. That includes us.
If we bind them into one seal, someone has to guard it for the rest of their life. I'll do it if that's your choice.
You could also keep one and give me three. I would know, but I wouldn't stop you.
Put one in your pack again. Feel that? Four of them are on one stone now. I do not want to learn what happens by morning.

choices.text: Shatter all four keys on the shrine stone
choices.conclusion: The metal shears like slate, and the ground answers: dust at the crossroads stands up wearing a mason's mark. The Sage writes one word in his ledger and steps back.

choices.text: Give the Sage all four keys to bind
choices.conclusion: He works until dawn folding four keys into one seal and hangs it under his coat. "Now I'm the thing worth robbing," he says, and writes your name beside his.

choices.text: Palm one key. Hand over the other three.
choices.conclusion: He counts three keys twice and asks nothing. The fourth rides your pack, heavier every mile. Behind you, moss is already growing back over an empty socket.

pages.title: The Last Line
pages.scene: Mile marker on the north road
pages.speaker: Adjutant Denn
dialogue: Hold up. You're hard to find for someone this famous.
Adjutant Denn, Kage's office. This is a proposed Provision Nine: thirty days of curfew, searches, and seizure.
Enforcement wants a name the village already trusts. I wrote that you had not consented. The office returned it with your signature copied onto the last line.
That is not authorization. I brought the wet original so you could see the discrepancy before they call it yours.
Careful, the ink's wet.

pages.title: Objection Entered
pages.scene: The mile marker, both copies held side by side
pages.speaker: Player
dialogue: That is not my signature. Enter the objection on both copies before we move.
Denn writes REFUSED AT FIRST NOTICE across the forged line, dates it, and gives you the dry copy. The office already has the wet one.

pages.title: Week One
pages.scene: Guard post, first week of Provision Nine
pages.speaker: Adjutant Denn
dialogue: The copied endorsement went into force before you could reach the office. Week one: two carts of blasting oil, a forged-seal ring, a man with sixty gate passes under a false floor.
All real. I checked twice. I always check twice.
The square empties at dusk like a tide now. People wave at the patrols.
Tips are coming in. The pile is longer every morning. Nobody signs them.
We're out of stamp ink already. I've ordered more.

pages.title: Edged Instruments
pages.speaker: Meru
dialogue: Fourth night of curfew, the Tarn girl started her labor. Babies don't read decrees.
Patrol stopped me at the bridge. Forceps are 'edged instruments' now. They kept the kit.
The baby came anyway. Nine fingers gripping, one thumb in her mouth. Strong.
The Tarns paid me through the window. My name went in a book at the gate.
The boy who wrote it down was polite. That's the part I keep chewing on.

pages.title: The Renewal
pages.speaker: Adjutant Denn
dialogue: Renewal form. Same clauses, plus two: paid tips, and seizure extends to 'known associates.'
Week one we pulled blasting oil off a cart. Week four we took a midwife's forceps. Same clause. Same stamp.
The office calls it the quietest month on record. Quiet is being paid for. I can't find the account it comes out of.
You want to know what the seat is, from down here? Whoever's name is on the last line. They used yours for a month; you never gave it.
Anyway. Form's on the table.

choices.text: Read the seizure clauses aloud in the square, then tear them.
choices.conclusion: Denn watches you read and does not stop you; the crowd keeps the torn halves like receipts. By dusk three sealed doors are open, and the Kage's office files your name under a different heading.

choices.text: Enforce the curfew only; copy every seizure into three ledgers.
choices.conclusion: One ledger to the office, one to the archive, one that never leaves your person. Denn adds his signature to all three without being asked.

choices.text: Sign the renewal and add names of your own.
choices.conclusion: The new names go up at the well by morning, yours at the bottom as author. Denn stamps the form and requests reassignment the same day; the tips triple overnight, still unsigned.

events.title: The Last Road Before the Seat

pages.title: Forty Behind Her
pages.speaker: Suma
dialogue: Hold on. Suma, from the southbound camp. We have not met; your road notices reached us before you did.
There are forty of us walking behind me, give or take. We chose to come because the next commitment deserves witnesses.
If %pet needs water, my youngest packed an extra skin. That is hospitality, not a debt.
Some came to cheer you. Some came because cheering makes them nervous. I told them both reasons could walk at the same pace.
Nobody sent us. I want that said plain. Nobody sent us.
We just want to stand where it happens. My feet already agreed.

pages.title: The Woman on the Stone
pages.scene: A rest stone, half a mile on
pages.speaker: Verah
dialogue: I'm not moving off this stone. You can go around.
My sister carried water for the last one who took a seat. Right up to the end, she carried it.
So. When someone like you wins, what happens to someone like me?
Don't answer fast. The fast answer is the one they've all had.
There's a second stone past the willow. If you wanted to sit and not say anything.

pages.title: Standard Language
pages.speaker: Undersecretary Corvel
dialogue: Undersecretary Corvel, joint provisioning office. I'll be brief. You're clearly making time.
The councils drafted terms. Recognition of the seat, supply lines, the gate guard stands down. Standard language.
Sign, and this stops being an uprising and starts being an administration.
Article nine, assets and instruments of the seat convey as-is. Boilerplate. Don't read it on the road.
The woman on the stone back there. People like her prefer paper. So do we.
Keep the pen either way. We order them by the crate.

pages.title: The Last Mile
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: The keeper at the waystation changes the horses without asking who they're for.
Suma's forty are singing something with no words to it, in shifts, badly.
Corvel's contract lies open on the table, weighted with the pen.
Verah walked as far as the last milestone. No further, she said. She is still there.

choices.text: Ask Suma's forty to walk in front, where everyone can see
choices.conclusion: Suma passes the word back and the singing stops; the counting starts instead, and it includes you. Corvel's clerk writes 'declined' in the margin and underlines it twice.

choices.text: Sign Corvel's contract and keep the copy
choices.conclusion: Corvel countersigns without looking at your face and dates it twice, once for each archive. From the milestone, Verah watches you take the copy and does not wave.

choices.text: Tell the walkers to fall in and keep their eyes down
choices.conclusion: The column forms fast and quiet, the way a thing forms when it has been practiced. Verah is gone from her stone before you reach it; Suma stays at the back, still counting.

pages.title: The List
pages.scene: A mile marker outside the village gate
pages.speaker: Amra Tull
dialogue: You walk faster than your statue will. I've been at this marker since yesterday noon.
Amra Tull. Deputy of records. Formerly deputy. The office door is off its hinges.
I'm not here about the door.
Read this. I copied it off the well wall before someone could add my name to it.
Fourteen names. Clerks, mostly. Two gate guards. Hob Setter, who counts arena bets. A scribe who wrote what she was handed.
They drew a torch next to the sixth one.

pages.title: The Sixth Name
pages.speaker: Deni Cros
dialogue: She showed you the list? Good. Saves me the speech.
The sixth name registered my father. Registered. One word in a ledger and we owed the seat three harvests.
You cut the head off. We're doing the fingers.
Nobody's died. A door. A stall. Paint.
Ask her what she stamped, all those years. Ask her whose hand held the stamp.

pages.title: Habit
pages.scene: A burned stall by the arena gate
pages.speaker: Hob Setter
dialogue: Mind the ash. It gets in the ledgers, and then every page smells like this.
I kept the odds honest. That was the whole job. Winner paid, loser paid, the house took its cut for the seat.
I knew where the cut went. Everyone knew. Knowing wasn't a crime last month.
My daughter asks why we eat in the back room now.
I still balance the book every night. Nobody collects it anymore. Habit.

pages.title: What to Write
pages.scene: The empty square, under the notice board
pages.speaker: Amra Tull
dialogue: Fourteen names, one torch drawing, and a village watching to see what you are.
The council won't rule on it. They say it wants a Kage's word.
There is no Kage. There's you.
Deni's crowd meets at dusk. Hob's stall is the third thing they'll burn, and the first was practice.
Tell me what to write.

choices.text: Stand at Hob's stall at dusk, in the open.
choices.conclusion: Deni's crowd arrives, counts who is standing behind you, and thins out one lantern at a time. By morning Amra has posted a single line under the list: witnessed, and answered.

choices.text: Order tribunals: open hearings, published names, punishments with a ceiling.
choices.conclusion: Amra drafts it fast, like she has been carrying the wording for days. Deni signs on as first complainant, inside the rules, which is where you put him.

choices.text: Say nothing. Watch the square, and mark who bows first.
choices.conclusion: Hob's stall burns on schedule while you watch from the notice board. By week's end three of the fourteen have knelt to you in the street, and Amra has stopped meeting your eyes.
